## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## Problem

The `UserPromptSubmit` hook took **~11.4s** in this repo (9.8s of it system time), overshooting Claude Code's 30s hook timeout once the Go build cache was cold — e.g. right after 773db0d34 bumped Go to 1.26.5 and invalidated it.

Both seconds-scale costs were go-git's `Worktree.Status()`, measured here at **5.25s** against **0.013s** for `git status --porcelain`.

## Root cause

go-git's `gitignore.ReadPatterns` does not thread a parent directory's patterns into its recursive walk. Each recursive call rebuilds its pattern set from that directory's own ignore files, so the prune check only ever matches patterns declared by the directory being scanned.

**A rule prunes a subtree only when its target is a direct child of the `.gitignore` declaring it.** Our root-level `e2e/artifacts/` rule was one level too deep, so every `Status()` descended all ~15k artifact directories.

Verified against go-git `main` with the same 3,000-directory tree:

| root `.gitignore` rule | result |
|---|---|
| `big/` | **0ms** — pruned |
| `e2e/artifacts/` | **121ms** — full descent |

Reference git prunes both identically. A CPU profile of `Status()` shows **100% of samples inside `collectIgnorePatterns` → `ReadPatterns`**; the diff walk contributes nothing, because it receives the full union of patterns and prunes correctly.

## Changes

**1. Move the ignore rule to `e2e/.gitignore` as `artifacts/`** so it is a direct child of its declaring `.gitignore`. Semantically identical to git, which reports the directory as ignored either way.

**2. Add `gitrepo.Status(ctx, repo)`** as the single entry point for reading worktree status, with `gitrepo.WithStatusCache(ctx)` memoizing the walk. `handleLifecycleTurnStart` installs a cache: it runs before the agent acts and writes only under `.entire/` and `.git/`, so the status cannot change mid-hook. Previously `CapturePrePromptState` and the strategy's prompt attribution each paid for a full walk.

The cache is deliberately **not** installed on post-agent paths — `DetectFileChanges` on TurnEnd must observe the agent's edits. That constraint is documented on `WithStatusCache`.

**3. Make the entry point real** rather than aspirational: migrated the three remaining direct callers (`DetectFileChanges`, `checkCanRewindWithWarning`, `checkResetSafety`) and added a `forbidigo` rule alongside the existing `Reset`/`Checkout` ones. Behavior-preserving — without a cache in `ctx`, `gitrepo.Status` is exactly `worktree.Status()`.

**4. Documented both conventions** in `CLAUDE.md` under Git Operations, including the `.gitignore` placement rule.

## Results

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| hook wall time | 11.36s | **0.91s** |
| `Status()` | 5.25s | 0.045s |
| second `Status()` call | 5.18s | 0.015s (cache hit) |

## Upstream

[go-git#2284](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2284) (merged, unreleased — we are on `v6.0.0-alpha.5`, still the newest tag) cuts the blind ignore-file opens and would take `Status()` from 5.24s to 2.47s here, but does not address the pattern-inheritance gap. {"additions":1158,"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjcwNzQx","is_bot":false,"login":"Soph","name":"Stefan Haubold"},"baseRefName":"main","body":"> **Draft.** This adds and removes public API, which CONTRIBUTING lists under the [RFC process](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/tree/main/rfcs). Opening as a draft so the design and the measurements are reviewable; happy to write it up as an RFC instead if you would prefer that first.

Supersedes #2302, which fixed the same defect inside the existing flat-pattern design. Its own body argued for this approach once the numbers were in.

## API surface

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Added | `gitignore.Scope`, `NewScope`, `DirPatterns`, `RootPatterns`, `IgnoreFile`, `filesystem.Options.IgnoreScope` |
| Removed | `merkletrie/filesystem.Options.IgnoreMatcher` — present in `v6.0.0-alpha.5` but never in a stable release, so not a compatibility break ([#2048](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2048)) |
| Deprecated | `gitignore.ReadPatterns` (unchanged behaviour) |

## The problem

`Status` collected every ignore pattern in the worktree before diffing, then matched every entry against that one flat list. Two consequences.

**It cannot express an excluded parent.** gitignore(5): a file cannot be re-included once a parent directory of it is excluded. A flat list has nowhere to record that, so a negation anywhere in the repository can re-include a path git ignores:

```
.gitignore:  outer/ignored/
             !outer/ignored/keep.txt

$ git check-ignore -v outer/ignored/keep.txt
.gitignore:1:outer/ignored/	outer/ignored/keep.txt
```

git attributes the verdict to the rule that excluded the parent and ignores the negation. `main` reports `keep.txt` as not ignored.

**It walks the worktree twice** — once to gather patterns, once to diff — and the first walk descended into ignored trees the second one then skipped.

## The design

`gitignore.Scope` carries the patterns in effect for one directory *together with whether that directory is excluded*. `Descend` derives a subdirectory's scope; once excluded it stays excluded and `Match` answers without consulting a pattern, so a negation below cannot win.

`Descend` takes the subdirectory's own patterns as a function, not a slice, and does not call it when the subdirectory is excluded — the decision not to read an ignore file below an excluded directory lives in one place where a caller cannot get it wrong.

The noder resolves each directory's scope from the `ReadDir` listing it already takes, so `.gitignore` is opened only in directories actually visited and never below an excluded one, and the separate collection pass is gone.

This is git's structure. `prep_exclude` keeps a prefix-keyed `exclude_stack`, aborts before reading a directory's `.gitignore` when that directory already matched unless the match was a negation, and `last_matching_pattern` short-circuits on the excluded ancestor rather than recomputing it per query ([dir.c](https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/dir.c)).

## Numbers

`Status`, versus `main`:

| | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StatusNestedIgnoredDir` 2000 ignored dirs | 252.1ms | **2.4ms** (-99.0%) |
| `StatusManyIgnoreFiles` 500 ignore files | 88.2ms | **52.5ms** (-40.4%) |
| `StatusLarge` 5000 files, no `.gitignore` | 23.1ms | **13.4ms** (-41.9%) |

`main` fails to scale on the first: ten times the directories cost it thirteen times the wall clock. The other two are shapes where pruning alone cannot help, since nothing is excluded wholesale — the saving there is the removed traversal and the smaller pattern set each entry is tested against.

Two of these benchmarks are new; the pre-existing `BenchmarkStatusIgnoredDir` could not show any of it, because its rule names a direct child of the root and its ignored tree is 21 directories wide.

`tests/gitcompare` measures the same shapes against the git binary. Read against its `Baseline/EmptyRepo` case, which is what a git *process* costs before it looks at a file (~11ms on macOS, a few on Linux):

| | git wall | git less baseline | go-git |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NestedIgnoredDir` | 12.1ms | ~1.2ms | 1.9ms |
| `ManyIgnoreFiles` | 33.1ms | ~22ms | 72.5ms |
| `LargeNoIgnoreFiles` | 18.8ms | ~8ms | 17.7ms |

## What this does not fix

`ManyIgnoreFiles` is still ~3x git's compute. Profiling says that is not the ignore machinery — reading the 500 `.gitignore` files is 22%, and git reads them too. The rest is elsewhere:

- **37% is `ObjectStorage.EncodedObject`**, one tree object per directory for the HEAD↔index diff. It scales with directory count, not file count: 1.4% at 20 directories, 37% at 500. go-git decodes the index's cache-tree extension into `idx.Cache` (`index/decoder.go:320`) but never reads it, so it redoes work git's cache-tree lets it skip.
- **95% of total time is syscalls**, `os.doInRoot` alone ~46%: every open goes through `BoundOS`/`os.Root`, which revalidates each path component. That is the deliberate symlink-safety boundary, but it means several syscalls where git pays one.

Both look worth their own issues; neither belongs here.

## Tests

- `gitignore`: `Scope` unit tests covering excluded-parent precedence, that `Descend` never reads an ignore file below an excluded directory, ordering, and the degenerate roots.
- `merkletrie/filesystem`: the nine existing ignore tests move to `IgnoreScope`, plus two the flat matcher could not express — a rule in a subdirectory's `.gitignore`, and a tracked entry forcing descent into an excluded directory where a negation must still not re-include a sibling. I checked the latter fails if excluded-parent precedence is removed.
- root: `Status` compared against `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` over six layouts. **This found a real bug** — the root scope was omitted when the root declared no patterns, so a worktree whose only rules live below the root reported ignored files as untracked. Fixed in the same series.

Only pre-existing failure is `TestConformanceSuite/TestIgnoreDoubleStarPrefix`, which fails on `main` too (git 2.50.1). `golangci-lint` v2.11.4 reports 0 issues repo-wide, and every commit builds and tests independently.

## AI assistance disclosure

Per [AI_POLICY.md](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md), produced with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5), disclosed with an `Assisted-by:` trailer on each commit. Behaviour was verified against reference git two ways: oracle tests comparing `Status` and pattern verdicts against the git binary, and by reading `prep_exclude` in git's `dir.c` to confirm the design matches.

{"additions":1158,"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjcwNzQx","is_bot":false,"login":"Soph","name":"Stefan Haubold"},"baseRefName":"main","body":"> **Draft.** This adds and removes public API, which CONTRIBUTING lists under the [RFC process](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/tree/main/rfcs). Opening as a draft so the design and the measurements are reviewable; happy to write it up as an RFC instead if you would prefer that first.

Supersedes #2302, which fixed the same defect inside the existing flat-pattern design. Its own body argued for this approach once the numbers were in.

## API surface

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Added | `gitignore.Scope`, `NewScope`, `DirPatterns`, `RootPatterns`, `IgnoreFile`, `filesystem.Options.IgnoreScope` |
| Removed | `merkletrie/filesystem.Options.IgnoreMatcher` — present in `v6.0.0-alpha.5` but never in a stable release, so not a compatibility break ([#2048](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2048)) |
| Deprecated | `gitignore.ReadPatterns` (unchanged behaviour) |

## The problem

`Status` collected every ignore pattern in the worktree before diffing, then matched every entry against that one flat list. Two consequences.

**It cannot express an excluded parent.** gitignore(5): a file cannot be re-included once a parent directory of it is excluded. A flat list has nowhere to record that, so a negation anywhere in the repository can re-include a path git ignores:

```
.gitignore:  outer/ignored/
             !outer/ignored/keep.txt

$ git check-ignore -v outer/ignored/keep.txt
.gitignore:1:outer/ignored/	outer/ignored/keep.txt
```

git attributes the verdict to the rule that excluded the parent and ignores the negation. `main` reports `keep.txt` as not ignored.

**It walks the worktree twice** — once to gather patterns, once to diff — and the first walk descended into ignored trees the second one then skipped.

## The design

`gitignore.Scope` carries the patterns in effect for one directory *together with whether that directory is excluded*. `Descend` derives a subdirectory's scope; once excluded it stays excluded and `Match` answers without consulting a pattern, so a negation below cannot win.

`Descend` takes the subdirectory's own patterns as a function, not a slice, and does not call it when the subdirectory is excluded — the decision not to read an ignore file below an excluded directory lives in one place where a caller cannot get it wrong.

The noder resolves each directory's scope from the `ReadDir` listing it already takes, so `.gitignore` is opened only in directories actually visited and never below an excluded one, and the separate collection pass is gone.

This is git's structure. `prep_exclude` keeps a prefix-keyed `exclude_stack`, aborts before reading a directory's `.gitignore` when that directory already matched unless the match was a negation, and `last_matching_pattern` short-circuits on the excluded ancestor rather than recomputing it per query ([dir.c](https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/dir.c)).

## Numbers

`Status`, versus `main`:

| | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StatusNestedIgnoredDir` 2000 ignored dirs | 252.1ms | **2.4ms** (-99.0%) |
| `StatusManyIgnoreFiles` 500 ignore files | 88.2ms | **52.5ms** (-40.4%) |
| `StatusLarge` 5000 files, no `.gitignore` | 23.1ms | **13.4ms** (-41.9%) |

`main` fails to scale on the first: ten times the directories cost it thirteen times the wall clock. The other two are shapes where pruning alone cannot help, since nothing is excluded wholesale — the saving there is the removed traversal and the smaller pattern set each entry is tested against.

Two of these benchmarks are new; the pre-existing `BenchmarkStatusIgnoredDir` could not show any of it, because its rule names a direct child of the root and its ignored tree is 21 directories wide.

`tests/gitcompare` measures the same shapes against the git binary. Read against its `Baseline/EmptyRepo` case, which is what a git *process* costs before it looks at a file (~11ms on macOS, a few on Linux):

| | git wall | git less baseline | go-git |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NestedIgnoredDir` | 12.1ms | ~1.2ms | 1.9ms |
| `ManyIgnoreFiles` | 33.1ms | ~22ms | 72.5ms |
| `LargeNoIgnoreFiles` | 18.8ms | ~8ms | 17.7ms |

## What this does not fix

`ManyIgnoreFiles` is still ~3x git's compute. Profiling says that is not the ignore machinery — reading the 500 `.gitignore` files is 22%, and git reads them too. The rest is elsewhere:

- **37% is `ObjectStorage.EncodedObject`**, one tree object per directory for the HEAD↔index diff. It scales with directory count, not file count: 1.4% at 20 directories, 37% at 500. go-git decodes the index's cache-tree extension into `idx.Cache` (`index/decoder.go:320`) but never reads it, so it redoes work git's cache-tree lets it skip.
- **95% of total time is syscalls**, `os.doInRoot` alone ~46%: every open goes through `BoundOS`/`os.Root`, which revalidates each path component. That is the deliberate symlink-safety boundary, but it means several syscalls where git pays one.

Both look worth their own issues; neither belongs here.

## Tests

- `gitignore`: `Scope` unit tests covering excluded-parent precedence, that `Descend` never reads an ignore file below an excluded directory, ordering, and the degenerate roots.
- `merkletrie/filesystem`: the nine existing ignore tests move to `IgnoreScope`, plus two the flat matcher could not express — a rule in a subdirectory's `.gitignore`, and a tracked entry forcing descent into an excluded directory where a negation must still not re-include a sibling. I checked the latter fails if excluded-parent precedence is removed.
- root: `Status` compared against `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` over six layouts. **This found a real bug** — the root scope was omitted when the root declared no patterns, so a worktree whose only rules live below the root reported ignored files as untracked. Fixed in the same series.

Only pre-existing failure is `TestConformanceSuite/TestIgnoreDoubleStarPrefix`, which fails on `main` too (git 2.50.1). `golangci-lint` v2.11.4 reports 0 issues repo-wide, and every commit builds and tests independently.

## AI assistance disclosure

Per [AI_POLICY.md](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md), produced with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5), disclosed with an `Assisted-by:` trailer on each commit. Behaviour was verified against reference git two ways: oracle tests comparing `Status` and pattern verdicts against the git binary, and by reading `prep_exclude` in git's `dir.c` to confirm the design matches.

10	// Status is the single entry point for reading go-git worktree status; the
11	// forbidigo rule in .golangci.yaml keeps callers off worktree.Status directly.
12	//
13	// go-git's Worktree.Status() is expensive: it walks the whole worktree twice
14	// (once collecting .gitignore patterns, once diffing), and gitignore.ReadPatterns
15	// does not thread a parent directory's patterns into its recursive walk, so it

18	// whole subtree walked: a single call cost 5.25s in this repo before e2e's
19	// artifacts rule moved into e2e/.gitignore.
20	
21	type statusCacheKey struct{}
22	
23	type statusCache struct {
24		mu       sync.Mutex
25		statuses map[string]git.Status
26	}
27	
28	// WithStatusCache returns a context that memoizes Status results.
29	//
30	// Install it only across a window that neither writes tracked files nor stages
31	// anything — otherwise later callers observe a stale status. Staging counts:
32	// .git/index lives inside .git/, but the index feeds the status diff, so an
33	// index write invalidates a cached result just as a worktree write does. Entire
34	// performs no index writes today (no SetIndex calls; the git subcommands on the
35	// hook paths are all index-read-only), which is what makes turn start a valid
36	// window. A hook that runs after the agent has edited files is not.
37	func WithStatusCache(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
38		return context.WithValue(ctx, statusCacheKey{}, &statusCache{
39			statuses: make(map[string]git.Status),
40		})
41	}
42	
43	// Status returns the worktree status for repo, reusing a cached result when ctx
44	// carries a cache from WithStatusCache and the same worktree was already read.
45	//
46	// The returned map is shared with other callers holding the same cached ctx, so
47	// callers must treat it as read-only.
48	func Status(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) (git.Status, error) {
49		worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
50		if err != nil {
51			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // callers add their own context
52		}
53	
54		cache, ok := ctx.Value(statusCacheKey{}).(*statusCache)
55		if !ok {
56			return worktree.Status() //nolint:wrapcheck,forbidigo // the sanctioned call site
57		}
58	
59		// Key on the worktree root rather than the repository pointer: callers on
60		// the same hook path open the repository independently.
61		root := worktree.Filesystem().Root()
62	
63		cache.mu.Lock()
64		defer cache.mu.Unlock()
65	
66		if cached, hit := cache.statuses[root]; hit {
67			return cached, nil
68		}
69	
70		status, err := worktree.Status() //nolint:forbidigo // the sanctioned call site
71		if err != nil {
72			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // callers add their own context
73		}
74		cache.statuses[root] = status
75	
76		return status, nil

input.old_string:
`Worktree.Status()` walks the whole worktree twice — once in
`gitignore.ReadPatterns` collecting patterns, once diffing. `ReadPatterns` does
**not** thread a parent directory's patterns into its recursive walk: each
recursive call rebuilds its pattern set from that directory's own ignore files,
so the prune check only ever matches patterns declared by the directory being
scanned.

**Consequence for `.gitignore` layout:** a rule prunes a subtree only when its
target is a *direct child* of the `.gitignore` declaring it. A root-level
`e2e/artifacts/` rule is one level too deep and never prunes, so every
`Status()` descended ~15k artifact directories and cost 5.25s (against 0.013s
for `git status --porcelain`), which timed out agent hooks. The rule therefore
lives in `e2e/.gitignore` as `/artifacts/`. When adding a new ignored directory,
declare it in a `.gitignore` in its parent directory rather than as a nested
path from the root — reviewers should flag multi-component directory patterns
added to the root `.gitignore`.

Anchor the relocated pattern with a leading slash. Moving `a/b/` to a
`.gitignore` in `a/` as bare `b/` also drops git's root anchoring, so it would
newly match `b` at any depth below `a/`; `/b/` preserves the original scope and
prunes identically.
input.new_string:
`Worktree.Status()` walks the worktree, so its cost scales with working-set size
rather than with the size of the change being inspected. It is the most expensive
git read on the hook paths, which is why it has a single entry point that can
memoize it.

**`.gitignore` placement no longer affects pruning.** It used to: go-git's
`gitignore.ReadPatterns` rebuilt its pattern set from each directory's own ignore
files without threading a parent's patterns into the recursive walk, so a rule
pruned a subtree only when its target was a *direct child* of the `.gitignore`
declaring it. A root-level `e2e/artifacts/` rule was one level too deep, so every
`Status()` descended ~15k artifact directories and cost 5.25s, timing out agent
hooks. [go-git#2309](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2309) replaced the
flat pattern list with per-directory `gitignore.Scope`, which inherits a parent's
patterns and short-circuits on an excluded ancestor, so both placements now prune
identically. Declare ignored directories wherever is clearest; the rule for
`e2e/artifacts` stays in `e2e/.gitignore` because that reads well next to the
directory it covers, not because it has to.

That fix also brought go-git's ignore semantics in line with git's on
excluded-parent precedence: a negation can no longer re-include a path below an
excluded directory. This repo declares no negation patterns, so nothing here
depended on the old behaviour.

When anchoring a directory rule inside a nested `.gitignore`, keep the leading
slash. Writing `a/b/` as bare `b/` in `a/.gitignore` drops git's root anchoring
and newly matches `b` at any depth below `a/`; `/b/` preserves the original
scope.

Author: Stefan Haubold <stefan@entire.io>

    perf: stop go-git walking ignored e2e/artifacts on every hook
    
    The UserPromptSubmit hook took ~11.4s in this repo (9.8s of it system
    time), overshooting Claude Code's 30s hook timeout once the Go build
    cache was cold.
    
    Both seconds-scale costs were go-git's Worktree.Status(), measured at
    5.25s here against 0.013s for `git status --porcelain`.
    
    Cause: gitignore.ReadPatterns does not thread a parent directory's
    patterns into its recursive walk. Each recursive call rebuilds its
    pattern set from that directory's own ignore files, so the prune check
    only ever matches patterns declared by the directory being scanned.
    A rule prunes a subtree only when its target is a direct child of the
    .gitignore that declares it. The root-level "e2e/artifacts/" rule was
    one level too deep to ever prune, so every Status() descended all
    15k artifact directories. Verified against go-git main: with the same
    3000-directory tree, a root "big/" rule prunes in 0ms while a root
    "e2e/artifacts/" rule costs a full descent.
    
    Two changes:
    
    - Move the rule to e2e/.gitignore as "artifacts/", making it a direct
      child of its declaring .gitignore. Identical semantics to git, which
      reports the directory as ignored either way.
    - Add gitrepo.Status, which memoizes the walk when the context carries
      a cache from gitrepo.WithStatusCache. TurnStart installs one: it runs
      before the agent acts and only writes under .entire/ and .git/, so
      the status cannot change mid-hook. CapturePrePromptState and the
      strategy's prompt attribution previously paid for one full walk each.
    
    Hook wall time: 11.36s -> 0.91s. The second Status() call is now a
    cache hit at 0.015s. Artifacts were left in place and grew to 15,742
    subdirectories during the test run with no regression.
    
    go-git#2284 (merged, unreleased; we are on v6.0.0-alpha.5) cuts the
    blind ignore-file opens and would take Status() from 5.24s to 2.47s

(open entry points) and `gitrepo/reftable.go` (`reftableStorer`).

#### Reading Worktree Status - Always Use `gitrepo.Status`

**Never call go-git's `worktree.Status()` directly.** Use
`gitrepo.Status(ctx, repo)`; a `forbidigo` rule in `.golangci.yaml` enforces
this, and `gitrepo/status.go` is the only sanctioned call site.

`Worktree.Status()` walks the worktree, so its cost scales with working-set size
rather than with the size of the change being inspected. It is the most expensive
git read on the hook paths, which is why it has a single entry point that can
memoize it.

**`.gitignore` placement does not affect pruning — but this depends on the pinned
go-git.** Before
[go-git#2309](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2309), `gitignore.ReadPatterns`
rebuilt its pattern set from each directory's own ignore files without threading a
parent's patterns into the recursive walk, so a rule pruned a subtree only when its
target was a *direct child* of the `.gitignore` declaring it. The root-level
`e2e/artifacts/` rule was one level too deep, so every `Status()` descended ~15k
artifact directories and cost 5.25s, timing out agent hooks; the rule had to live
in `e2e/.gitignore` as a workaround. #2309 replaced the flat pattern list with
per-directory `gitignore.Scope`, which inherits a parent's patterns and
short-circuits on an excluded ancestor, so nested rules prune correctly and the
workaround is gone.

The `go.mod` requirement on go-git is what keeps that true: Go will not downgrade
below it, so every ordinary build has the fix. A deliberate `replace` or explicit
downgrade to a pre-#2309 go-git brings the seconds-per-hook cost back — if hooks
suddenly feel slow after pointing go-git at a local checkout, this is why.

#2309 also brought go-git's ignore semantics in line with git's on excluded-parent
precedence: a negation can no longer re-include a path below an excluded directory.
This repo declares no negation patterns, so nothing here depended on the old
behaviour.

`gitrepo.WithStatusCache(ctx)` memoizes the walk for callers that read status
more than once. Install it **only** across a window that neither writes tracked

content.text:
The race-enabled suite is still building (race builds are slow here). While it finishes, here's where this landed.

## What go-git#2309 changes for us

Your PR replaced the flat pattern list with per-directory `gitignore.Scope`, so patterns inherit down the walk and an excluded ancestor short-circuits. Two consequences for the CLI:

**1. The #1911 workaround is now dead weight.** I verified this against the real repo rather than assuming — reverted the rule to root-level `e2e/artifacts/`, built an 8001-directory artifacts tree, and measured:

| go-git | `Status()` |
|---|---|
| `v6.0.0-alpha.5` (current pin) | **1.279s** ← #1911's bug, reproduced |
| `main` (post #2309) | **23.3ms** |
| reference `git status --porcelain` | 20ms |

23.3ms matches the empty-tree number (24.5ms), so the subtree is fully pruned. go-git is now at parity with git.

**2. It's faster even with nothing to prune.** Steady-state `Status()` on this repo went 60.9ms → 24.5ms (-60%), from the removed second traversal — that win applies to every user's repo, not just ours.

## What I did

Full revert of the workaround, as you suggested:

- `go.mod` → `v6.0.0-alpha.5.0.20260812095450-22b9459b2be0` (main tip, your #2313 merge)
- `.gitignore` → `e2e/artifacts/` restored, byte-exact to the pre-#1911 blob
- `e2e/.gitignore` → deleted
- `CLAUDE.md` + `status.go` → the placement rule and its "reviewers should flag multi-component root patterns" guidance are gone; kept a short note on *why* `gitrepo.Status`/`WithStatusCache` exist

What makes the full revert safe is the `go.mod` floor: Go won't silently downgrade below it, so every ordinary build has the fix. Getting the old behaviour back takes a deliberate `replace` — relevant to you specifically, since pointing go-git at a local pre-#2309 checkout will bring the seconds-per-hook cost back. I documented that as the symptom to recognise.

I kept `gitrepo.Status`, the `forbidigo` rule, and `WithStatusCache`. The cache's value scales with the user's working-set size, not ours — for a large customer repo two walks vs one is still worth avoiding, and the staleness footgun is documented and structurally contained to TurnStart.

## Verified

`mise run test` (8825 tests), `mise run test:ci` (exit 0), canary 4/4 — and a nice incidental: the canary generated 384 real artifact directories, which `git status` correctly ignores via `.gitignore:53`. `go mod tidy` is a no-op on the tree.

Two caveats: `golangci-lint` reports 2 pre-existing `goconst` issues in `cmd/entire/cli/plugin_fetch.go` (byte-identical to `origin/main`, from `f727a8a31` — raw `"http"`/`"https"` where `login.go` has the consts). Not from this change, but your local lint gate is currently red on main. And the `lint:gomod` task fails only because it greps `git status` for an uncommitted `go.mod`; it passes once committed.

## One decision for you

The pin is a **pseudo-version** — you're the go-git maintainer, so cutting `v6.0.0-alpha.6` and re-pinning to the tag is available and is a one-line follow-up. Shipping a stable CLI release against an untagged dep is a bit awkward for reproducibility/SBOM. I'll commit the pseudo-version once the race suite lands unless you'd rather tag first.

perf: adopt go-git's scoped ignore walk, drop the .gitignore workaround

Bumps go-git to main for go-git#2309, which replaces the flat ignore-pattern
list with per-directory gitignore.Scope. Patterns now inherit down the walk and
an excluded ancestor short-circuits, so a rule prunes its subtree regardless of
which .gitignore declares it.

That removes the constraint 6ddce4747 worked around. The root-level
"e2e/artifacts/" rule was one level too deep for the old flat walk and never
pruned, so every Worktree.Status() descended all of e2e/artifacts. The rule had
to move to e2e/.gitignore; it no longer does, so the layout goes back to what it
was before that commit and e2e/.gitignore is removed.

Measured against this repo with an 8001-directory e2e/artifacts tree and the
root-level rule restored:

    v6.0.0-alpha.5   1.279s   (the pre-fix behaviour, reproduced)
    main (#2309)     23.3ms
    git status       20.0ms

23.3ms matches the empty-tree measurement, so the subtree is fully pruned.
#2309 also removes the second traversal, which helps where nothing is excluded
wholesale: steady-state Status() on this repo goes 60.9ms -> 24.5ms. That part
benefits every repo, not just ones with a large ignored tree.

The go.mod requirement is what keeps the layout safe: Go will not downgrade
below it, so every ordinary build has the fix. A deliberate replace directive
pointing go-git at a pre-#2309 checkout brings the per-hook cost back, which
CLAUDE.md now names as the symptom to recognise.

#2309 additionally aligns go-git with git on excluded-parent precedence: a
negation can no longer re-include a path below an excluded directory. This repo
declares no negation patterns and the CLI authors none, so nothing here depended
on the old behaviour.

gitrepo.Status, the forbidigo rule, and WithStatusCache stay. Status() cost
scales with working-set size, so sparing a second walk is worth more in a large
user repo than it is here, and the staleness constraint is documented and
structurally limited to TurnStart.

The pin is a pseudo-version at main tip; re-pinning to a v6.0.0-alpha.6 tag is a
one-line follow-up once one is cut.

plugin_fetch.go:59:7: string `https` has 3 occurrences, but such constant `schemeHTTPS` already exists

Any package-counting linter (goconst, dupl, maintidx) can only be caught after the fact. Checking out the PR merge commit instead would catch this class before merge, at the cost of the run depending on main moving underneath the PR.
Verification
mise run fmt && mise run lint → 0 issues. mise run test:ci passes.

Main is red on lint: two `goconst` errors in `cmd/entire/cli/plugin_fetch.go`.

```
plugin_fetch.go:59:7: string `https` has 3 occurrences, but such constant `schemeHTTPS` already exists
plugin_fetch.go:61:7: string `http`  has 3 occurrences, but such constant `schemeHTTP`  already exists
```

`login.go:25-26` already declares `schemeHTTP` and `schemeHTTPS` for this package, so the literals just need to use them. This changes three call sites:

- `plugin_fetch.go:59,61` — `case "https":` / `case "http":`

- `plugin_fetch.go:124` — `u.Scheme != "https" && u.Scheme != "http"`

- `review_target.go:142` — the same comparison

## Why it only broke after the merge

`goconst` counts occurrences per package, with a threshold of 3. The literals were split across two files that never existed at the same time until the merge:

| Commit | plugin_fetch.go | review_target.go | occurrences of `"https"` | lint | |---|---|---|---|---| | main before merge (`6e7985f4e`) | 2 | absent | 2 | pass | | trail branch head (`b989d612c`) | absent | 1 | 1 | pass | | merge (`f6fd1159d`) | 2 | 1 | 3 | fail |

Both parents were genuinely green. The trail branch last merged main at `fbbff047` on Aug 10, 08:38; `plugin_fetch.go` landed on main at `18f9bcd9d` (PR #1422) on Aug 10, 21:42 — 13 hours later. Nothing in the two diffs overlaps, so git merged cleanly and only the merged package hit 3.

Two things worth noting for later:

1. `goconst` blamed `plugin_fetch.go`, which the merge never touched. The new code was `review_target.go`.

2. `.github/workflows/lint.yml` checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, so the merged tree is never linted before it lands. Any package-counting linter (`goconst`, `dupl`, `maintidx`) can only be caught after the fact. Checking out the PR merge commit instead would catch this class before merge, at the cost of the run depending on main moving underneath the PR.

## Verification

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` → 0 issues. `mise run test:ci` passes.

`checkpoint rewind --list` was the observability mechanism for many checkpoint tests, so removing the command required reworking them:

Review complete. Here it is.

# Review: PR #1747 — Remove long-deprecated commands and aliases

**Overview.** Deletes CLI surface that has carried deprecation notices for a while: `entire reset`, `entire rewind`, `entire checkpoint rewind`, and the hidden top-level shortcuts `resume`/`attach`/`explain`/`trace`. Takes `rewind.go` (~1,220 lines), `reset.go`, `aliascmd.go`, `TruncateTranscriptAtUUID`/`writeTranscript`, and the tests that used `checkpoint rewind --list` as an observability hook. −4,875/+236 across 43 files.

The direction is right and the execution is mostly careful. My substantive concern is what's left *behind*, not what's removed.

## What's solid

- **Migration targets verified real.** `entire clean --session <id>` and `entire clean -a/--all` both exist, so the documented `reset` replacement actually works.
- **The `deprecated_strings_test.go` guard was correctly left alone.** It sweeps production strings for deprecated forms and deliberately skips comment lines. Keeping the now-removed forms in its list is the right call — it prevents reintroduction.
- **`agent-help` needs no change** because it renders live from the Cobra tree, so the agent-advertised surface self-updates. Worth noting explicitly since a removal PR usually leaves stale agent docs.
- **The test *adaptations* are stronger than what they replaced.** `default_branch_test.go` goes from `len(points) != 1` to asserting shadow-branch existence, the file's actual content on that branch, and the specific `tasks/<id>/checkpoint.json` path. That's a better test.
- **`sanitizeForTerminal`'s move into `checkpoint_list.go` is byte-faithful** — same codepoint ranges, same logic.
- **Several deleted tests were worth less than zero.** `TestAgentSessionIDTransformation` tested nothing about session-ID transformation: its body simulated hooks, then did `t.Skip("no rewind points created")` — silently skipping the exact failure it should catch — then called `Rewind`. And `TestShadow_UntrackedFilesAcrossMultipleSessions` shipped with unresolved contradictory reasoning (`// Actually, it was created before the checkpoint... // Let me reconsider the test logic...`) and a `t.Log` where an assertion belonged. Deleting these is a net gain, and I'd say so in the PR body rather than filing them under "rewind tests".

## Findings

**1. The retained strategy machinery loses its execution-level safety coverage.** `strategy.Rewind` and `manual_commit_rewind.go` stay, and `strategy/rewind_test.go` survives — but that file only covers the *planning* path: `TestShadowStrategy_PreviewRewind` asserts `preview.FilesToDelete` excludes a pre-existing untracked file. The two execute-path tests (`Rewind_FromSubdirectory`, `Rewind_FromRepoRoot`) contain no untracked/ignored assertions at all. The deleted `TestShadow_GitignoredFilesPreservedDuringRewind` and `TestShadow_UntrackedFilePreservation` were the only tests asserting those files actually survive *on disk* after a rewind runs.

Not a live risk — no CLI caller can reach it. But per CLAUDE.md the hazard (go-git's `Reset`/`Checkout` deleting ignored dirs, "would destroy `.entire/`") lives precisely in the execution path, and it's now unguarded. Keeping unreachable code with weakened tests is the worst of the three options; I'd either pull the strategy removal into this PR or retain one execute-path test.

**2. `GetRewindPoints` is still live — the PR description overstates the orphaning.** `checkpoint_list.go:50` and `:86` still call it for `checkpoint list --pending`. Only `Rewind()` is CLI-orphaned. This matters for scoping the follow-up PR.

**3. CLAUDE.md still documents rewind as a Strategy capability with no note that it's unreachable.** The strategy section keeps `GetRewindPoints()` / `Rewind()` — List and restore to checkpoints and "Rewind restores files from shadow branch commit tree". Accurate but incomplete — add a line saying there's no CLI surface, or the next agent to read this will assume there is one.

**4. Six files carry doc comments naming commands that no longer exist.** `resume_picker.go:68`, `attach.go:55`, `session/state.go:259`, `review/marker_fallback.go:14,37,125`, `review_helpers.go:11` all say `entire attach`; `claudecode/claude.go:237` says "Used for task checkpoint rewind." Before this PR those named a hidden-but-working command; now they name nothing. The guard test exempts comments by design, so nothing catches them. Cheap fix to `entire session attach`.

**5. No CHANGELOG entry for a breaking removal.** CHANGELOG.md is untouched, and this is the PR that most needs it. Compounding it: cobra's "Did you mean?" won't map `reset` → `clean` (no string similarity), so the migration pointer the deprecation message used to give disappears exactly when users need it. Consider a one-release hidden stub that errors with the pointer, or at minimum a Breaking section in the changelog.

**6. Unrelated dependency bump bundled in.** `.opencode/package-lock.json` jumps `@opencode-ai/plugin`/`sdk` 1.4.7 → 1.14.28 — ten minor versions, unrelated to command removal. Drop it from this PR. Separately: that lockfile seems to churn spontaneously during test runs (I hit the identical modification in an unrelated session today), so it probably wants pinning or ignoring on its own ticket.

**7. README's replacement framing may overpromise.** The bullet becomes "**Recover instantly** — resume from a known-good checkpoint", and "Non-destructive rewind — restore files from any checkpoint" is deleted. But `session resume` resumes the *session*, not the *files* — I confirmed no remaining CLI path restores files from a checkpoint. A user reading "recover instantly" will likely expect file recovery. Either say plainly that file recovery is now manual (checkout from the shadow branch), or drop the "recover" framing.

**8. Nit:** the adapted `default_branch_test.go` lost the "exactly one checkpoint" property — the old `len(points) != 1` would catch a duplicate-checkpoint regression; existence + content won't. You already use session `StepCount` elsewhere in this PR; adding it here restores it.

## On the product decision

Cursor's High Risk label is fair. After this PR, checkpoints are inspectable (`explain`, `search`) but not restorable through any command. That's a real capability removal, not just an alias cleanup — worth an explicit sign-off in the PR rather than inheriting it from the old deprecation notice, since the notice said "will be removed" without saying "and nothing replaces it."

One process note: the PR reports `TestExplainCmd_PositionalArgConflictsWithFlags` / `..._SummaryTimeoutSecondsValidation` failing because the repo's own `.entire/settings.local.json` has `enabled: false`. That's correctly identified as pre-existing and unrelated, but a test whose outcome depends on developer-local settings is a latent flake for everyone — worth its own issue.

The direction is right and the execution is mostly careful — migration targets check out (`entire clean --session <id>` and `-a/--all` both exist), the `deprecated_strings_test.go` guard was correctly left in place, `agent-help` needs no change because it renders live from the Cobra tree, and the `sanitizeForTerminal` move into `checkpoint_list.go` is byte-faithful.

Worth calling out that several deleted tests were worth less than zero, which I'd say in the PR body rather than filing them under "rewind tests": `TestAgentSessionIDTransformation` tested nothing about session-ID transformation — its body simulated hooks, then `t.Skip("no rewind points created")`, silently skipping the exact failure it should catch, then called `Rewind`. And `TestShadow_UntrackedFilesAcrossMultipleSessions` shipped with unresolved contradictory reasoning (`// Actually, it was created before the checkpoint... // Let me reconsider the test logic...`) and a `t.Log` where an assertion belonged. Also, the `default_branch_test.go` adaptations are genuinely stronger than what they replaced — shadow-branch content and `tasks/<id>/checkpoint.json` paths beat a bare `len(points)` count.

My substantive concerns are about what's left behind, not what's removed.

**1. The retained strategy machinery loses its execution-level safety coverage.** `strategy.Rewind` and `manual_commit_rewind.go` stay, and `strategy/rewind_test.go` survives — but that file only covers the *planning* path: `TestShadowStrategy_PreviewRewind` asserts `preview.FilesToDelete` excludes a pre-existing untracked file. The two execute-path tests (`Rewind_FromSubdirectory`, `Rewind_FromRepoRoot`) contain no untracked/ignored assertions at all. The deleted `TestShadow_GitignoredFilesPreservedDuringRewind` and `TestShadow_UntrackedFilePreservation` were the only tests asserting those files actually survive *on disk* after a rewind executes.

Not a live risk, since no CLI caller can reach it. But per CLAUDE.md the hazard — go-git's `Reset`/`Checkout` deleting ignored directories, which "would destroy `.entire/`" — lives precisely in the execution path, and it is now unguarded. Retaining unreachable code with weakened tests is the worst of the three options; I'd either pull the strategy removal into this PR or keep one execute-path test.

**2. `GetRewindPoints` is still live, so the description slightly overstates the orphaning.** `checkpoint_list.go:50` and `:86` still call it for `checkpoint list --pending`. Only `Rewind()` is CLI-orphaned. Worth fixing in the description because it changes the scope of the follow-up PR.

**3. CLAUDE.md still documents rewind as a Strategy capability with no note that it is now unreachable.** The strategy section keeps ``GetRewindPoints()` / `Rewind()` - List and restore to checkpoints`` and "Rewind restores files from shadow branch commit tree". Accurate but incomplete — worth a line saying there is no CLI surface, or the next reader will assume there is one.

**4. Six files carry doc comments naming commands that no longer exist.** `resume_picker.go:68`, `attach.go:55`, `session/state.go:259`, `review/marker_fallback.go:14,37,125` and `review_helpers.go:11` all say `entire attach`; `claudecode/claude.go:237` says "Used for task checkpoint rewind." Before this PR those named a hidden-but-working command; now they name nothing. `deprecated_strings_test.go` exempts comment lines by design, so nothing catches these.

**5. No CHANGELOG entry for a breaking removal.** `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched, and this is the PR that most needs one. Compounding it: cobra's "Did you mean?" will not map `reset` to `clean` (no string similarity), so the migration pointer the deprecation message used to give disappears exactly when users hit it. Either a one-release hidden stub that errors with the pointer, or at minimum a Breaking section in the changelog.

**6. Unrelated dependency bump bundled in.** `.opencode/package-lock.json` moves `@opencode-ai/plugin`/`sdk` from 1.4.7 to 1.14.28 — ten minor versions, unrelated to command removal. Worth dropping from this PR. Separately, that lockfile appears to churn spontaneously during test runs (I hit the identical modification in an unrelated session today), so it probably wants pinning or ignoring on its own ticket.

One process note, not this PR's job: the two `TestExplainCmd_*` failures you identified as pre-existing come from the repo's own `.entire/settings.local.json` having `enabled: false`. A test whose outcome depends on developer-local settings is a latent flake for everyone and deserves its own issue.

Posted: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1747 — as a `COMMENTED` review (not request-changes, since you asked for the findings, not a verdict).

**On finding 7 — you were right, and I've dropped it.** I checked rather than argue: `resume.go:161` calls `CheckoutBranch`, and resume's own help text says it "checks out its branch, restores its checkpoint session log". So files genuinely move; only the *session log* comes from the checkpoint. My "no remaining CLI path restores files" was wrong.

What's actually lost is much narrower than I stated: restoring the working tree to a *specific mid-session checkpoint*, including uncommitted intermediate state — intra-session granularity. Branch-level recovery survives, so README's "Recover instantly" is defensible, and they'd already deleted the checkpoint-granular claim ("Non-destructive rewind — restore files from any checkpoint"). Nothing worth flagging.

That also softens my "product decision" note from the earlier review, which leaned on the same wrong premise — so I left it out of the post. What went up is findings 1–6 plus a short framing of what's solid (migration targets verified, the guard test correctly untouched, `agent-help` self-updating, the faithful `sanitizeForTerminal` move) and the observation that two of the deleted tests were actively harmful — the `t.Skip("no rewind points created")` one that skipped its own failure mode, and the one with `// Let me reconsider the test logic...` left in. Those support Victor's deletions rather than questioning them, so worth him having in writing.

I also kept the `TestExplainCmd_*` note at the end, flagged as not his job — tests that depend on a developer's local `.entire/settings.local.json` will bite others.

Ranked by what I'd actually block on: **1** is the only one with teeth (retained-but-unreachable code whose execution-path safety net is gone — the `.entire/`-destruction hazard CLAUDE.md warns about). **5** is the user-facing one. **2, 3, 4, 6** are cleanups.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [0.9.0] - 2026-07-27

### Added

- `entire doctor migrate-checkpoints` migrates existing checkpoints from the git-branch backend to git-refs ([#1611](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1611))
- git-refs checkpoints can be discovered on a second device via remote enumeration, and `entire checkpoint list --json` gives a machine-readable listing (migrate off `rewind --list`) ([#1771](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1771), [#1768](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1768))
- Hidden `entire checkpoint resume` command ([#1701](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1701))
- `entire explain` streams live progress and reports an observable-state timeout diagnostic ([#964](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/964))
- `entire review`: live token counts for the Claude and Codex reviewers, and Codex now runs real skills via on-disk `$name` discovery and native invocation ([#1666](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1666), [#1669](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1669))
- Import gains imported sessions in `entire session list`, anchors imported checkpoints to the default-branch head, and warns when importing agent history while logged out ([#1699](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1699), [#1825](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1825), [#1774](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1774))
- `entire dispatch` gains local agent selection ([#1797](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1797))
- Transcript image externalization for Claude Code and Codex, plus capture of Cursor sidecar images ([#1589](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1589))
- Experimental commands are gated behind a build-time visibility flag — shown in developer/nightly builds, hidden in stable releases, always runnable ([#1703](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1703))
- `entire agent-help` teaches agents entire usage through worked examples and an injected first-turn invariant ([#1821](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1821))
- `entire doctor`/`entire status` warn when Claude Code hook config has drifted out of date ([#1808](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1808))
- The non-git `entire enable` bootstrap collapses into a single setup question ([#1818](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1818))
- `entire search` accepts multiple repos for semantic search ([#1845](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1845))

### Changed

- `entire search` now routes to the v4 query-serve path with cross-cell fan-out; the v3 path is removed ([#1800](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1800))
- New setups now default to git-refs checkpoint storage; the setup wizard keeps a checkpoint-storage question with git-refs recommended ([#1789](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1789), [#1799](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1799))
- `entire repo mirror list` now covers both mirrored and mirrorable repos in one listing, with per-cluster detail available via `mirror get` ([#1681](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1681))
- Root help output is grouped by user journey, and `--json` moves off the shared persistent flag onto the specific commands that support it ([#1745](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1745), [#1680](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1680))
- Checkpoints route through `entire://` push-through mirrors ([#1732](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1732))
- `entire status` no longer prints the strategy name ([#1793](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1793))
- Code-search results read more clearly in the terminal ([#1742](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1742))
- `entire repo clone` resolves `/gh/` shorthand via a pull-gated placement lookup ([#1779](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1779))
- The self-update plugin skips the post-plugin version check ([#1731](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1731))
- Display-only Repo read enums are loosened for forward compatibility ([#1663](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1663))

fix: address review findings on the deprecated-command removal

Follow-ups from the review of #1747, plus the lint failures its CI run is
currently reporting.

Restore the execution-path safety net the removed tests were carrying.
strategy.Rewind stays in the tree with no CLI caller, and the deleted
integration tests were the only ones asserting that gitignored files survive a
rewind actually running; strategy/rewind_test.go only covers PreviewRewind, the
plan. That matters because per CLAUDE.md the go-git hazard — Reset/Checkout
deleting ignored directories, which would take out .entire/ — lives in the
execution half. TestShadowStrategy_Rewind_PreservesIgnoredFiles now covers it,
creating the ignored files after the test's own HardReset so it exercises Rewind
rather than that reset. Writing it confirmed the property holds today.

Note it deliberately asserts nothing about untracked files: deletion is driven by
SessionState.UntrackedFilesAtStart, so with no session state every untracked file
reads as created-since-the-checkpoint and is removed. That direction is
PreviewRewind's territory.

Document that Rewind() has no CLI surface, so the next reader does not take it
for a supported entry point, and record which half of its behaviour each test
covers. GetRewindPoints() is still live — checkpoint list --pending calls it —
so only the restore path is orphaned.

Point the stale doc comments at the commands that still exist. Six files named
`entire attach`, which was hidden-but-working before this branch and is now
nothing at all; deprecated_strings_test.go exempts comment lines by design, so
nothing catches these. claudecode.FindCheckpointUUID's comment cited task
checkpoint rewind as its consumer; it has no production caller left, which is
worth saying where someone will read it.

Drop the unrelated @opencode-ai/plugin and sdk bump (1.4.7 -> 1.14.28) back to
main's pinned version; it is ten minor versions of unrelated churn in a command
removal.

Fix the two goconst failures and silence maintidx in manual_commit_workflow_test.go.
Lint has been failing on this branch in CI: the "package main" literals had
existing pkgFuncA/pkgFuncB constants in testconsts.go with byte-identical values,
and TestShadow_FullWorkflow crossed the maintidx threshold once the
shadow-branch assertions replaced the rewind observations. The nolint carries a
reason, matching how the repo handles the same linter elsewhere.

Verified: mise run lint reports 0 issues tree-wide, and mise run test:ci passes.

## What went in

**Finding 1** — added `TestShadowStrategy_Rewind_PreservesIgnoredFiles`. It creates the ignored files *after* the test's own `HardReset`, since go-git's hard reset is itself one of the calls that deletes ignored dirs — writing them earlier would have tested the wrong step.

Writing it turned up something: **my first version failed, and my assumption was the wrong part.** The ignored files (`.entire/settings.json`, `debug.log`) survived fine; the untracked `scratch.txt` got deleted. That's by design — deletion is driven by `SessionState.UntrackedFilesAtStart`, so with no session state every untracked file reads as created-since-the-checkpoint. So the test now deliberately asserts nothing about untracked files and says why. The `.entire/`-survival property holds today, and is now pinned.

496	#### Reading Worktree Status - Always Use `gitrepo.Status`
497	
498	**Never call go-git's `worktree.Status()` directly.** Use
499	`gitrepo.Status(ctx, repo)`; a `forbidigo` rule in `.golangci.yaml` enforces
500	this, and `gitrepo/status.go` is the only sanctioned call site.
501	
502	`Worktree.Status()` walks the worktree, so its cost scales with working-set size
503	rather than with the size of the change being inspected. It is the most expensive
504	git read on the hook paths, which is why it has a single entry point that can
505	memoize it.
506	
507	**`.gitignore` placement does not affect pruning — but this depends on the pinned
508	go-git.** Before
509	[go-git#2309](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2309), `gitignore.ReadPatterns`
510	rebuilt its pattern set from each directory's own ignore files without threading a
511	parent's patterns into the recursive walk, so a rule pruned a subtree only when its
512	target was a *direct child* of the `.gitignore` declaring it. The root-level
513	`e2e/artifacts/` rule was one level too deep, so every `Status()` descended ~15k
514	artifact directories and cost 5.25s, timing out agent hooks; the rule had to live
515	in `e2e/.gitignore` as a workaround. #2309 replaced the flat pattern list with
516	per-directory `gitignore.Scope`, which inherits a parent's patterns and
517	short-circuits on an excluded ancestor, so nested rules prune correctly and the
518	workaround is gone.
519	
520	The `go.mod` requirement on go-git is what keeps that true: Go will not downgrade
521	below it, so every ordinary build has the fix. A deliberate `replace` or explicit
522	downgrade to a pre-#2309 go-git brings the seconds-per-hook cost back — if hooks
523	suddenly feel slow after pointing go-git at a local checkout, this is why.
524	
525	#2309 also brought go-git's ignore semantics in line with git's on excluded-parent
526	precedence: a negation can no longer re-include a path below an excluded directory.
527	This repo declares no negation patterns, so nothing here depended on the old
528	behaviour.

73		}

91		if err != nil {

102		}
103	
104		var selected string
105		form := NewAccessibleForm(
106			huh.NewGroup(

108					Title("Resume a session").
109					Description("Checks out the branch, restores the session log, and offers to start the agent.\n" +
110						"Lists sessions from this machine — to resume a branch from origin, run: entire session resume <branch>").
111					Options(options...).
112					Value(&selected),
113			),
114		)

116			// User cancelled (esc/Ctrl+C) or the context was cancelled — exit cleanly
117			// without a noisy error.

122		}
123

126			return nil
127		}
128	
129		idx, convErr := strconv.Atoi(selected)

131			return fmt.Errorf("invalid selection %q", selected)
132		}
133		chosen := items[idx]
134	
135		if !chosen.isResumable() {
136			fmt.Fprintf(w, "Session %s can't be resumed: %s.\n", chosen.state.SessionID, chosen.unresumableReason())

138		}
139

141		// a second checkout here. Point the user at that worktree and tell them to
142		// re-run the picker there — that preserves the selected-session flow (the
143		// picker resumes the exact session by its checkpoint), whereas suggesting

185	func countImportedSessions(states []*strategy.SessionState) int {

191		}

193	}

198		if s.EndedAt != nil {
199			return *s.EndedAt
200		}
201		if s.LastInteractionTime != nil {
202			return *s.LastInteractionTime
203		}
204		return s.StartedAt

## What

Bumps go-git to main for [go-git#2309](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2309), which replaces the flat ignore-pattern list with per-directory `gitignore.Scope`. Patterns now inherit down the walk and an excluded ancestor short-circuits, so a rule prunes its subtree regardless of which `.gitignore` declares it.

That removes the constraint #1911 worked around, so the workaround is reverted: `e2e/artifacts/` goes back to the repository root `.gitignore` (byte-identical to the pre-#1911 blob) and `e2e/.gitignore` is deleted.

## Why the revert is safe

Measured against this repo with an 8001-directory `e2e/artifacts` tree and the root-level rule restored:

| go-git | `Status()` |
|---|---|
| `v6.0.0-alpha.5` (the current pin) | **1.279s** — the #1911 bug, reproduced |
| `main` (post-#2309) | **23.3ms** |
| reference `git status --porcelain` | 20.0ms |

23.3ms matches the measurement with no artifacts present, so the subtree is fully pruned rather than merely cheaper. Reference `git check-ignore` attributes the ignore to the root rule, and a canary run during verification generated 384 real artifact directories that `git status` correctly ignored.

#2309 also removes the second traversal, which helps in repos where nothing is excluded wholesale: steady-state `Status()` here went **60.9ms → 24.5ms**. That half benefits every user's repo, not just ones with a large ignored tree.

The `go.mod` requirement is what keeps the layout safe going forward: Go will not downgrade below it, so every ordinary build has the fix. A deliberate `replace` pointing go-git at a pre-#2309 checkout brings the per-hook cost back, which `CLAUDE.md` now names as the symptom to recognise.

## Correctness, not just speed

#2309 additionally aligns go-git with git on excluded-parent precedence: a negation can no longer re-include a path below an excluded directory, which is what gitignore(5) specifies and what `git check-ignore` reports. This repo declares no negation patterns and the CLI authors none, so nothing here depended on the old behaviour.

## Dependency delta

The pin is a pseudo-version at go-git `main` tip (`22b9459b2be0`). The whole non-test delta over `v6.0.0-alpha.5` is confined to the ignore/status machinery — `plumbing/format/gitignore/`, `utils/merkletrie/filesystem/node.go`, `worktree.go`, `worktree_status.go` — plus `x/crypto` and `x/text` patch bumps that come along with it. Nothing near transport, packfiles, refs, or object storage. go-git's own `go` directive is unchanged.

`merkletrie/filesystem.Options.IgnoreMatcher` was removed upstream in favour of `IgnoreScope`; the CLI never referenced it, so there is no call-site change here.

**Open question:** re-pinning to a `v6.0.0-alpha.6` tag once one is cut would be preferable to shipping a stable release against a pseudo-version. That is a one-line follow-up.

## What is kept

`gitrepo.Status`, the `forbidigo` rule, and `WithStatusCache` all stay. `Status()` cost scales with working-set size, so sparing a second walk is worth more in a large user repo than it is here, and the staleness constraint is documented and structurally limited to TurnStart.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run lint` — 0 issues tree-wide
- [x] `mise run test:ci` — real exit 0 (unit + integration under `-race`, 84 packages, zero FAIL/DATA RACE lines), canary 56 + 4
- [x] `Status()` re-measured on this repo before/after, and against reference git
- [x] Placement verified irrelevant post-#2309 on a synthetic 3000-directory tree (root rule 528µs vs nested 378µs; on `alpha.5` the same root rule costs 1.076s)

per-directory `gitignore.Scope`, which inherits a parent's patterns and
short-circuits on an excluded ancestor, so nested rules prune correctly and the
workaround is gone.

}

    fi
    t1=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())')

    ms=$(python3 -c "print(($t1-$t0)*1000)")
    total=$(python3 -c "print($total+$ms)")
    n=$((n+1))

}

echo "size|config|hook_avg_ms|walks|cache_hits|avg_walk_ms"
for size in 1500 20000; do
  dir=$S/bench-repo-$size
  make_repo "$dir" "$size"
  # warm caches
  printf '{"session_id":"warm","transcript_path":"","prompt":"warm"}' \

  echo "$size|cache ON |$(echo "$out_on" | cut -d'|' -f2-)"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measures what gitrepo.WithStatusCache saves on the TurnStart hook.

Interleaves cache-on / cache-off runs so page-cache warming and machine drift hit
both arms equally, resets per-run session state so every run does the same work,
and reports medians.
"""
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time

S = pathlib.Path("/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-soph--herdr-worktrees-cli-worktree-clear-cloud-548a/ac065b40-422f-4c60-bd54-24f1e1606b6d/scratchpad")
BIN = str(S / "entire-instr")
RUNS = 9
WARMUP = 3

BASE_ENV = dict(os.environ)
BASE_ENV.update({
    "ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR": str(S / "bench-config"),
    "XDG_CACHE_HOME": str(S / "bench-cache"),
    "ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE": "file",
    "ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH": str(S / "bench-tokens"),
    "ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE": str(S / "bench-authstore"),
    "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY": "0",
})


def sh(args, cwd=None, env=None):
    return subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, env=env or BASE_ENV,
                          stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def make_repo(dir_: pathlib.Path, nfiles: int):
    if dir_.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(dir_)
    dir_.mkdir(parents=True)
    sh(["git", "init", "-q"], cwd=dir_)
    for k, v in (("user.name", "t"), ("user.email", "t@t"), ("commit.gpgsign", "false")):
        sh(["git", "config", k, v], cwd=dir_)
    per = 50
    for i in range(nfiles):
        d = dir_ / "src" / f"pkg{i // per}"
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (d / f"f{i}.go").write_text(f"package p\n\nfunc F{i}() {{}}\n")
    sh(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=dir_)

**The cache is not obsolete — keep it.** The data says it earns its place, more than I'd have guessed.

**It saves exactly one full worktree walk per turn.** Structurally confirmed: 1.00 walk/run with the cache, 2.00 without, and 1.00 hit/run. The two callers on that path (`CapturePrePromptState` and the strategy's prompt attribution) each want status independently.

**Internal consistency check passes,** which is what makes me trust the numbers: at 20k files the hook delta is 430.0 − 310.2 = **119.8ms**, and the median walk is **119.1ms**. The saving is precisely one walk, not a measurement artifact. Same at 1,500 files: 12.3ms delta vs an 11.3–12.1ms walk. And the walk cost itself is identical in both arms (119.1ms), so the only thing differing is call count.

**The value scales with the user's working set, not ours:**
- 1,500 files → saves ~12ms of ~207ms (**~6%**)
- 20,000 files → saves ~120ms of 430ms (**~28%**)

This repo is 1,411 files, so locally it's marginal — which is probably what prompted your question. But go-git#2309 didn't change the number of walks, only their cost, so the cache's saving stayed proportional. On a 20k-file monorepo it's an eighth of a second on every single prompt.

I had to redo the measurement: my first pass ran cache-ON first and it absorbed the cold page-cache cost, producing the nonsense result of ON being *slower* with a 589ms walk vs 127ms. Interleaving the arms per iteration, resetting session state so every run does identical work, and taking medians fixed it.

**One thing worth considering** rather than keep-or-delete: the cache exists only because two code paths in different packages (`state.go` and `strategy/common.go`) each read status. Threading the value explicitly from `lifecycle.go` would be exactly as fast with no staleness footgun at all. That's a signature change across a package boundary, which is presumably why the context cache was chosen — but it's the option that gets the 120ms *and* removes the sharp edge, if the footgun is what bothers you.

content.content:
#### Reading Worktree Status - Always Use `gitrepo.Status`

**Never call go-git's `worktree.Status()` directly.** Use
`gitrepo.Status(ctx, repo)`; a `forbidigo` rule in `.golangci.yaml` enforces
this, and `gitrepo/status.go` is the only sanctioned call site.

`Worktree.Status()` walks the worktree, so its cost scales with working-set size
rather than with the size of the change being inspected. It is the most expensive
git read on the hook paths, which is why it has a single entry point that can
memoize it.

`gitrepo.WithStatusCache(ctx)` memoizes the walk for callers that read status
more than once. Install it **only** across a window that neither writes tracked
files nor stages anything: the TurnStart hook qualifies (it runs before the agent
acts and writes only session metadata under `.entire/` and refs under `.git/`),
post-agent hooks such as TurnEnd do not — `DetectFileChanges` there must observe
the agent's edits.

Staging counts as invalidation even though `.git/index` sits inside `.git/`: the
index feeds the status diff, so an index write makes a cached result stale. Entire
performs no index writes today — there are no `SetIndex` calls, the single
`Storer.Index()` use (`strategy/content_overlap.go`) is a read, and the git
subcommands on the hook paths are all index-read-only. **If you add an
index-mutating operation, check whether it lands inside a status-cache window.**
The cache is context-scoped to one short-lived hook process, so it cannot go
stale across turns.

git add -A && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
perf: drop the worktree-status cache

gitrepo.WithStatusCache memoized Worktree.Status() for the TurnStart hook, where
CapturePrePromptState and the strategy's prompt attribution each read status.
Measured, it saved exactly one walk per hook — 1 walk per run with it, 2 without
— worth ~12ms of a ~207ms hook on a 1.5k-file tree and ~120ms of a 430ms hook on
a 20k-file one.

Real, but it is a cache: correct only inside a window that writes no tracked
files and stages nothing, enforced by a hand-maintained allowlist of lifecycle
events plus an ordering constraint in handleLifecycleTurnStart (EnsureSetup
hoisted above the first read because it can rewrite the tracked
.entire/.gitignore). Every new lifecycle event and every new index-mutating
operation had to be checked against that precondition, forever, and a mistake
there means handlers silently acting on a stale worktree view. The latency did
not justify carrying that standing hazard.

gitrepo.Status stays as the single entry point, along with the forbidigo rule
that keeps callers off worktree.Status — that is worth keeping on its own, and it
is where a caller-threaded status would land if the walk cost ever needs
reclaiming. Callers that need status twice in one hook should read it once and
pass it down.

The ordering in handleLifecycleTurnStart is kept: running strategy setup before
the first status read still means the pre-prompt snapshot describes the tree the
agent starts from, rather than one setup is about to change. Only the
cache-consistency rationale is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

`gitrepo.WithStatusCache` was the other half of #1911's mitigation. Measured on the TurnStart hook, it saved exactly one `Status()` walk per hook (1 walk/run with it, 2 without, 1 cache hit/run):

| tracked files | cache | hook median | walks/run | median walk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,500 | on | 194.6ms | 1.00 | 12.1ms |
| 1,500 | off | 206.9ms | 2.00 | 11.3ms |
| 20,000 | on | **310.2ms** | 1.00 | 119.1ms |
| 20,000 | off | **430.0ms** | 2.00 | 119.1ms |

The hook delta at 20k files (430.0 − 310.2 = 119.8ms) matches the median walk (119.1ms), so the saving is precisely one walk. Arms were interleaved per iteration with per-run state resets, because running them sequentially let the first arm absorb cold page-cache cost and inverted the result.

So it was worth real latency — ~28% of that hook on a 20k-file tree. It is still removed, because it is a cache: correct only inside a window that writes no tracked files and stages nothing, enforced by a hand-maintained allowlist of lifecycle events plus an ordering constraint in `handleLifecycleTurnStart`. Every new lifecycle event and every new index-mutating operation had to be checked against that precondition indefinitely, and a mistake means handlers silently acting on a stale worktree view. That standing hazard was not judged worth the latency.

`gitrepo.Status` and the `forbidigo` rule stay — worth keeping on their own, and the natural home for a caller-threaded status if the walk cost ever needs reclaiming. Callers needing status twice in one hook should read once and pass it down. The `handleLifecycleTurnStart` ordering is kept for its own reason (the pre-prompt snapshot should describe the tree the agent starts from); only the cache-consistency rationale is gone.
"""

marker = "## What is kept"
assert marker in body, "anchor not found"
body = body.replace(marker, section.strip() + "\n\n## What is kept")

# The "what is kept" paragraph named WithStatusCache; correct it.
body = body.replace(
    "`gitrepo.Status`, the `forbidigo` rule, and `WithStatusCache` all stay. `Status()` cost scales with working-set size, so sparing a second walk is worth more in a large user repo than it is here, and the staleness constraint is documented and structurally limited to TurnStart.",
    "`gitrepo.Status` and the `forbidigo` rule stay. Every worktree-status read still funnels through one sanctioned call site, which is what makes the cost measurable and gives a caller-threaded status somewhere to live later.")
p.write_text(body)
print("body updated;", "WithStatusCache" in body and "still references WithStatusCache (expected in the new section)" or "no stale refs")

content.text:
Cache removed. #1968 is now `4c3a6d343`, **+33/−322** across 10 files — two commits: the go-git bump, then the cache removal.

What went with it: `WithStatusCache`/`statusCache`, the `statusCacheSafe` allowlist in `lifecycle.go`, and both cache-only test files. `gitrepo.Status` and the `forbidigo` rule stay — one sanctioned call site is worth having regardless, and it's where a caller-threaded status would go if you ever want the 120ms back.

Three things the removal turned up that needed handling:

**The `gitrepo` import in `lifecycle.go` became unused** — the cache was its only consumer there. Build caught it.

**Two comments justified things purely in cache terms.** `explain_repo.go` cited `WithStatusCache` as its example of a context-scoped value. More interesting, `handleLifecycleTurnStart` had a comment explaining why `EnsureSetup` is hoisted above the first status read — framed entirely as cache consistency. The *ordering* still has value without the cache (the pre-prompt snapshot should describe the tree the agent starts from, not one setup is about to change), so I kept the hoist and rewrote the rationale. Deleting the comment wholesale would have left a load-bearing ordering looking arbitrary.

**I rebased onto current main.** Local lint was red with the two `plugin_fetch.go` `goconst` issues — the branch predated #1966. Not from my change, but it meant local verification didn't match what CI tests on the merge ref. Rebasing fixed that: lint 0 issues, `test:ci` real exit 0, canary 60 + 4.

CLAUDE.md's status section is now +9/−37 — it keeps the measured walk costs (~12ms at 1.5k files, ~120ms at 20k) and the "read once, pass it down" guidance, and records that the absence of memoization is deliberate with the number it costs. That last part is the bit worth having: without it someone re-adds the cache in six months having re-derived the same 28%.

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Exact text to drop: `// Shared with the turn-start pre-prompt capture via the context status cache, so the expensive go-git worktree walk runs once per hook rather than once per caller.`

**2. `.golangci.yaml:117`**
- summary: The `forbidigo` message is a third copy of the perf rationale and still states the reverted claim.
- cost: It says `Worktree.Status() walks ignored subtrees (seconds in this repo)` — the premise this diff reverts (`e2e/artifacts/` back in the root `.gitignore`) and contradicts (`~120ms on a 20k-file tree`). Two divergent numbers for the same fact in the same tree.
- use instead: Keep the message to the rule (`use gitrepo.Status(ctx, repo)`) and let `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/status.go:12-15` be the single place that states the cost.

**3. `cmd/entire/cli/state.go:430` (`getUntrackedFilesForState`)**
- summary: Re-implements the untracked-file extraction that `DetectFileChanges` already does, including its own repo open and worktree walk.
- cost: Identical loop and identical filter (`st.Worktree == git.Untracked` + `shouldIgnoreSessionTrackingPath`). Previously the two shared one walk through the context cache; with the cache gone each is a separate full walk, so the duplication became a duplicated *cost*, not just duplicated code. - summary: The new comment prescribes "read it once per hook and pass the result down," but nothing in the diff provides the plumbing, and TurnStart still reads status twice.
- cost: On TurnStart, `CapturePrePromptState` → `getUntrackedFilesForState` (`state.go:116`) and `InitializeSession` → `calculatePromptAttributionAtStart` (`manual_commit_hooks.go:2505`) each do a full walk. - use instead: Pass the already-computed `git.Status` from the pre-prompt read into `calculatePromptAttributionAtStart` (and give `DetectFileChanges`/`getUntrackedFilesForState` a status-accepting variant). Honest caveat: this crosses the `cli` → `strategy` package boundary via `InitializeSession`'s signature, so it is real work — but without it the new comment is aspirational.

content.content:
#### Reading Worktree Status - Always Use `gitrepo.Status`

**Never call go-git's `worktree.Status()` directly.** Use
`gitrepo.Status(ctx, repo)`; a `forbidigo` rule in `.golangci.yaml` enforces
this, and `gitrepo/status.go` is the only sanctioned call site.

`Worktree.Status()` walks the worktree, so its cost scales with working-set size
rather than with the size of the change being inspected — measured at ~12ms on a
1.5k-file tree and ~120ms on a 20k-file one. It is the most expensive git read on
the hook paths, so read it once per hook and pass the result down rather than
calling `gitrepo.Status` again. There is deliberately no memoization: a
context-scoped cache previously saved one walk per TurnStart hook (~28% of that
hook on a 20k-file repo), but it had to be kept out of any window that writes
tracked files or stages anything, and that standing staleness hazard was not
judged worth the latency.
